segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics digest from November 23, 2026.
Today we cover big news, including Genesis AI's funding, a laundry robot success, and advances in autonomous driving.
From Robotics & Automation News, Genesis AI raises five hundred million dollars in Series A funding at a three and a half billion dollar valuation to advance general-purpose robotics.
The company intends to utilize these funds to expand robot production, enhance data collection, and recruit personnel.
Genesis is increasing the manufacturing of its general-purpose robot, the Eno, with a focus on expanding into new sectors such as hospitality and healthcare.
The company develops an integrated platform which incorporates the GENE AI foundation model and the Genesis World simulation platform.
Long term, the objective is the creation of robots capable of autonomous, multi-step tasks across diverse environments.
This investment signals a significant push toward tangible, general-purpose physical automation.
From Robotics & Automation News, Gobano Robotics reports 99.5 percent success rate for autonomous laundry robot.
This report details the performance of an autonomous laundry robot at the Henri Wartner Group, achieving a ninety-nine point five percent success rate in its operation.
The system autonomously handles repetitive towel folding and inspection tasks over several hours.
Through reinforcement learning, the robot achieves sixty-eight percent of a human worker's throughput during an eighteen-hour shift.
The robot demonstrates the ability to automatically recover from grasp failures to maintain production flow without continuous human supervision.
Production data is utilized to continuously improve the robot's performance, with plans for future capability expansion underway.
This development indicates continued advancement in applying artificial intelligence to complex, repetitive industrial tasks.
From Robotics & Automation News, Kakao Mobility partners with Nvidia to develop Level 4 autonomous driving technology.

This report details an agreement between Kakao Mobility and Nvidia to develop Level 4 autonomous driving technology, focusing on integrating autonomous driving software with advanced computing and sensor systems.
The collaboration involves merging Kakao Mobility's autonomous driving software with Nvidia's computing, sensor, and safety technologies.
Kakao Mobility intends to develop a high-performance computing unit utilizing Nvidia Drive AGX Thor processors and the Hyperion architecture.

This partnership is designed to establish the technical foundation for driverless mobility services within South Korea by advancing end-to-end artificial intelligence technology and preparing for Level 4 commercialization.
This development signals a significant step toward the practical implementation of advanced autonomous driving systems.
From Robotics & Automation News, Remedy Robotics raises sixty-two million dollars to advance an AI-powered cardiovascular surgery robot.
This funding supports clinical trials, regulatory approval, and further development of the robotic platform for remote and potentially autonomous endovascular operations.
The N1 System utilizes robotics, machine learning, and computer vision to analyze imaging and simulate procedures.
Remedy Robotics plans pivotal clinical trials with the University of California as the company pursues FDA approval for neurovascular intervention.
The development focuses on using the robotic platform to analyze complex data and simulate intricate procedures.
The goal of the work is to expand access to specialist treatment globally through this robotic system.
This development signals progress in integrating advanced artificial intelligence into complex medical procedures.
From Robotics & Automation News, Nvidia expands Isaac robotics platform with new humanoid and AI development tools.
This report details the expansion of the Isaac robotics platform through the introduction of new simulation frameworks, AI training tools, datasets, and a reference humanoid robot.
The expansion includes the Agile ONE SN platform from Agile Robots, which integrates Nvidia's Isaac GR00T foundation model and Jetson Thor.
Furthermore, Nvidia released Isaac OS and Isaac Lab 3.0, along with resources such as the Human 1M Dataset for robot learning.
European robotics companies are currently integrating these Nvidia technologies into their development platforms.
This development highlights the industry trend of combining foundation models, simulation, and hardware for more adaptable autonomous systems.
The integration of these advancements signals a shift toward more unified and sophisticated autonomous system development across the sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, Mitsubishi Electric expands US manufacturing and technology investments to $2.9 billion.
This report details the company's substantial commitment of over two point nine billion dollars in investments, acquisitions, and commitments made within the United States over the last two years.

These investments include two hundred fifty-nine point five million dollars allocated to the development of manufacturing facilities across Kentucky, Pennsylvania, and Ohio, resulting in the creation of more than four hundred jobs.

Furthermore, the company is expanding into software and cybersecurity through planned acquisitions and the establishment of a new digital transformation hub, with specific projects focusing on the expansion of switchgear manufacturing and data-center cooling operations to strengthen US manufacturing capabilities in energy, cybersecurity, and artificial intelligence.
This strategic move indicates increased integration of advanced technology within the North American industrial landscape.
From Robotics & Automation News, Schunk spin-off Tactilia Robotics launches to develop dexterous robot hands, a development focused on creating modular robotic hands for industrial automation.

The company, based in Munich, is developing hands designed to reliably grip and manipulate objects across diverse robot platforms through the integration of mechanical engineering, sensors, actuators, software, and physical artificial intelligence.

Tactilia employs a modular approach which allows the hands to adapt to different industrial applications without imposing manufacturer restrictions, aiming for practical integration in industrial settings.
This methodology centers on achieving human-like dexterity by combining complex systems for reliable object handling.
The advancement signals a progression toward more versatile and adaptable physical manipulation in automated systems.
From Robotics & Automation News, European automakers expand autonomous driving programs with Nvidia technology.
This report details the integration of Nvidia technologies to advance autonomous driving capabilities across the European automotive sector.
European automakers including Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen, and Volvo are integrating Nvidia's Hyperion platform and AI software to support advanced driver assistance and autonomous driving levels.
Additionally, Bolt is developing a robotaxi program utilizing Nvidia's Alpamayo software with the objective of achieving commercial operations in Europe.
Initiatives are also underway to address autonomous freight and public transportation through collaborations involving companies like Einride and academic institutions.
Nvidia has introduced safety frameworks such as Halos SAFE and the Alpamayo 2 Edge model to facilitate development and ensure autonomous vehicle safety.
This development signifies a tangible progression in applying advanced artificial intelligence to real-world vehicle autonomy.

From Robotics & Automation News, Multiway Robotics showcases wheeled humanoid and autonomous forklifts at CeMAT Asia 2026, revealing five autonomous material handling solutions presented at the event.

The display included specialized vehicles such as an omnidirectional sideloader, a narrow-aisle forklift, an autonomous pallet truck, and a counterbalanced forklift, alongside a wheeled humanoid robot.
This robot demonstrated mobile manipulation capabilities intended for flexible handling within manufacturing and warehousing environments.
Furthermore, autonomous forklifts were showcased for applications in heavy transport, access to high-density warehousing, and precision stacking.
Multiway also presented integrated software platforms designed to coordinate these autonomous vehicles with overall warehouse operations.
This demonstration indicates advancements in integrating complex mobile robotics with existing logistics infrastructure.
The ongoing development suggests increased deployment potential for autonomous systems in logistics sectors.

From Robotics & Automation News, Boston Dynamics gave its Atlas humanoid robot wheels to test new reinforcement learning capabilities, and the experiment successfully evaluated motor performance under varied speed and torque demands.
Engineers attached scooter rims to the robot's ankle actuators to evaluate motor performance, a process designed to bridge the gap between simulated behaviors and real-world physical hardware.

The research involved combining motor control with reinforcement learning to develop more robust control systems, aiming to enhance Atlas's reliability in real-world environments rather than creating a fully wheeled robot.
This methodology focused on assessing the interaction between motor control and learned behaviors in physical motion.
The findings suggest a pathway for improving the adaptability and reliability of advanced robotic systems in physical settings.
From Humanoid.guide, Topstar unveils Star humanoid for factory handling tasks.

This report details the introduction of the Star humanoid, a 172 centimeter tall, 72 kilogram bipedal unit designed for factory material handling and sorting, boasting a combined payload capacity of ten kilograms across its two arms.
The unveiling occurred at TOPS DAY 2026, where Topstar integrated Star into a program that combines hardware with operational data collection for model training.
The development priorities for Star include the ability to sort varied products, perform multi-tasking at workstations, and execute intelligent material handling.
Furthermore, the company is testing Xiaotuo, a wheeled humanoid, for similar manufacturing applications.
This development indicates a focus on integrating physical robotics with data-driven machine learning for industrial automation.
From Robotics & Automation News, BlueBotics unifies fleet management for manual forklifts and mobile robots.

This update introduces a unified mission dispatch system allowing the ANT server software to assign tasks to Automated Guided Vehicles, Autonomous Mobile Robots, and forklifts based on real-time location and availability.
The system incorporates an in-cab interface enabling forklift operators to manage assignments and coordinate movement between manual and automated vehicles.
This coordination facilitates the prevention of traffic congestion and enhances warehouse space utilization through shared space awareness.
The system also supports pallet tracking and generates analytics such as heatmaps to identify operational inefficiencies.
This development signals increased integration and optimization within material handling technology for future industrial applications.
From Humanoids Daily, RoboStore Adds AGIBOT to Its U.S.
Lineup, With Humanoids From $29,999.
This report details the introduction of AGIBOT humanoids into the United States market by RoboStore, a distributor for Unitree.
The new offerings include the X2, A3, and G2 humanoids, with the X2 Neo starting at a price of twenty-nine thousand nine hundred ninety-nine dollars.
This expansion establishes a second major Chinese supplier for RoboStore alongside Unitree.
The company is currently concentrating efforts on localization initiatives specifically for these robotic systems within the U.S. market.
This development signals an increased diversification of available humanoid robotic systems for enterprise and research applications.
Industry observers are monitoring the progression of these localization efforts.
From Hackaday - Robots, "Soft Robot Made for the Races".
This story details a recent study indicating a slight increase in land speed records achieved by soft robotics.
The research employed pneumatic logic gates for actuation, which facilitated rapid cycling between abduction and adduction instead of relying on direct microcontroller control.
The robots demonstrated compliant oscillations that permit the use of alternative fluids such as water in their operation.

The physical construction of the robot utilized three-dimensional printing with thermoplastic elastomer, although further development is suggested focusing on silicone materials for future iterations.
This research demonstrates the evolving capabilities within the field of soft robotics.
This work points toward continued advancements in adaptable and fluid-driven robotic systems.
And that's all the circuits for today!
Genesis AI just powered up a massive funding round.
Thanks for plugging into the future with me.
Until tomorrow, keep building brilliantly!
